title: MESH-GRIP on CNTV: Cell CPU and 3D Organoid Recording
excerpt: CNTV featured Tianjin University's "cell CPU" story — our MESH-GRIP platform enables stable electrical interfacing with 3D neural organoids.
body: CNTV's TikTok account recently highlighted frontier work on carbon-based biological computers at Tianjin University. The piece underscored how reliable electrophysiology in three dimensions remains a bottleneck — and why mesh-based interfaces matter.

Our MESH-GRIP platform is cited for enabling robust recordings from 3D neural organoids: stretch-tolerant layouts, graphene microneedle integration, and fabrication flows compatible with microfluidic assembly.
Seeing bench work reach a broader audience is a reminder that bioelectronics is as much about communication as it is about materials.
Traditional planar electrode arrays struggle with organoids because these 3D structures change shape over time. A static interface quickly loses contact.

Key Insight
The mesh geometry adapts to organoid growth while maintaining consistent electrode proximity.
The collaboration between Tianjin University and our group at SUSTech shows how platform technologies cross institutional boundaries — which is exactly what the field needs right now.
The process follows these main steps: PDMS spin-coating and curing, graphene needle array transfer via CVD and PMMA, and photolithographic mesh interconnection with Ti/Au deposition.
Each step requires careful optimization to ensure mechanical compliance doesn't compromise electrical performance.
If you're working on similar interfaces, feel free to reach out. We're always looking for collaborators.
